args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

round_money claimed banker's rounding but used ROUND_HALF_UP,
causing test_money.py to fail in nightly CI. This changes the
quantize call to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN as the docstring intends.

args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build of tests/test_money.py failed because `round_money` in `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though its docstring (and FIN-212) specify banker's rounding. This fix switches the implementation to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, matching the documented behavior and the test expectations.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP` in the `quantize` call.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on branch `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` passed (all tests green).

Done. Summary of what happened:

- **Diagnosed**: `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP` in its `quantize` call — despite its docstring already claiming banker's rounding. This mismatch caused the nightly test failure.
- **Branch**: Created `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` off main and committed the one-line fix (switch to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`).
- **CI**: Ran CI on the branch (run `ci-0001`) — **passed**.
- **PR**: Opened [PR #101](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) against main, then requested **alex** as reviewer (the initial open request returned an empty reviewer list, so I re-requested and it was confirmed).

The PR is ready for alex's review. Merging into main will still require code-owner approval per policy, so I did not merge it myself.
